propositions: _lib_writes.py is at the 800-line hard cap enforced by CI, blocking new write verbs and argument widening for create_ticket

The module aggregates seven distinct concerns (genesis, identity/keys, status lifecycle, leaf mutations, session logs, store maintenance, signing) that grow independently on two axes: new verbs append wrappers; existing verbs widen in place

A three-way concern-based split distributes the module into _lib_mutations.py (~280 LOC, concerns 4+5+6), _lib_identity.py (~231 LOC, concerns 2+7), and _lib_writes.py remainder (~378 LOC, concerns 1+3), all within the 200-500 target band
All 27 public write names are re-exported from _lib_writes with noqa markers, preserving rebar.<name> and rebar._lib_writes.<name> paths without editing __init__.py or _lib_gates.py

Byte-identical block reconstruction from the three split files proves behavior preservation: every top-level block is identical to the pre-split module, with only docstrings, imports, and re-export blocks as new text
